rows.label: Android
rows.description: operating system created by Google for use on mobile devices
rows.hook: powers most of the world's smartphones and is symbolised by a little green robot

rows.label: macOS
rows.description: operating system for Apple computers
rows.hook: is the desktop system for a line of sleek laptops and desktops, with a dock along the screen edge

rows.label: Windows 11
rows.description: personal computer operating system by Microsoft released in 2021
rows.hook: brought a centered taskbar and rounded corners to the desktop, with strict hardware requirements

rows.label: ChromeOS
rows.description: Linux distribution developed by Google
rows.hook: is a lightweight system built around a web browser, common on low-cost school laptops

rows.label: iOS
rows.description: mobile operating system by Apple Inc.
rows.hook: runs the world's best-known smartphone line and debuted alongside it

rows.label: Steam
rows.description: video game store and digital distribution platform among other services
rows.hook: is the biggest storefront for PC games, famous for its huge seasonal sales

rows.label: Windows 10
rows.description: personal computer operating system by Microsoft that was released in 2015
rows.hook: was the successor that brought back the Start menu after a tile-based predecessor

rows.label: App Store
rows.description: digital app distribution platform for iOS/iPadOS
rows.hook: is where iPhone owners download software, with the maker taking a famous cut of each sale

rows.label: Ubuntu
rows.description: Linux distribution developed by Canonical
rows.hook: is a hugely popular Linux distribution whose name is a southern African word about humanity toward others

rows.label: Scratch
rows.description: programming language learning environment
rows.hook: teaches kids to code by snapping together colorful blocks, with a cat as its mascot

rows.label: Unreal Engine
rows.description: video game engine series developed by Epic Games
rows.hook: powers many blockbuster titles and is known for its photorealistic graphics

rows.label: MS-DOS
rows.description: Microsoft operating system
rows.hook: was the text-based command-line system that ran on early IBM-compatible PCs

rows.label: C#
rows.description: multi-paradigm (object-oriented) programming language
rows.hook: is an object-oriented language widely used for building games in Unity and business software

rows.label: TypeScript
rows.description: programming language, superset of JavaScript that compiles to JavaScript
rows.hook: adds static typing on top of JavaScript and compiles down to it

rows.label: React
rows.description: JavaScript library for building user interfaces
rows.hook: is a JavaScript library built around reusable components for making web interfaces

rows.label: Windows NT
rows.description: Microsoft operating system family
rows.hook: is the business-grade operating system family that underpins its maker's modern desktop systems

rows.label: Windows 8
rows.description: personal computer operating system by Microsoft that was released in 2012
rows.hook: replaced the Start menu with a full-screen grid of tiles that many users disliked

rows.label: SteamOS
rows.description: gaming Linux distribution
rows.hook: is the Linux-based system that powers a popular handheld gaming PC

rows.label: watchOS
rows.description: mobile operating system for Apple Watches
rows.hook: runs on a popular wrist-worn wearable that tracks fitness

rows.label: HarmonyOS
rows.description: operating system developed by Huawei
rows.hook: is a Chinese-made smartphone system positioned as an alternative to the leading mobile platforms

rows.label: Windows 98
rows.description: personal computer operating system by Microsoft
rows.hook: was the popular late-nineties desktop system that built the web browser into the shell

rows.label: Windows 2000
rows.description: personal computer operating system by Microsoft
rows.hook: was a business-focused system built on the NT kernel and praised for its stability

rows.label: PowerShell
rows.description: cross-platform command-line interface and scripting language for system and network administration
rows.hook: is a command-line tool and scripting language for automating system administration tasks

rows.label: Kali Linux
rows.description: Debian-derived Linux distribution
rows.hook: is a distribution packed with penetration-testing tools, favored by security professionals

rows.label: Classic Mac OS
rows.description: Apple Macintosh’s original operating system (1984–2002)
rows.hook: was the original graphical system that greeted users with a smiling computer icon at startup

rows.label: Kotlin
rows.description: general-purpose programming language derived from Java
rows.hook: is the modern language officially favored for building Android apps

rows.label: iPadOS
rows.description: mobile operating system of the iPad, developed by Apple Inc.
rows.hook: runs on a popular touchscreen tablet line

rows.label: Plan 9
rows.description: distributed operating system designed by Bell Labs as an UNIX's intended successor
rows.hook: was a research operating system meant to succeed Unix, named after a notoriously bad sci-fi movie

rows.label: tvOS
rows.description: operating system of the Apple TV
rows.hook: runs on a small streaming box that plugs into a television
